question: When a clip lands on a spot that already holds a clip, what should happen?
context: A dropped file covers what is under it, as Premiere does. A pasted clip, an Option-dragged copy and Add Media at Playhead go up onto a new track instead. A clip you drag along is refused with 'no room'. These were each built on their own over the last two weeks.

options.label: It covers what is there, every way in (Premiere)
options.summary: Dropping a file, pasting, Option-dragging a copy, dragging a clip and Add Media at Playhead all cover what is under them on that track, trimming or splitting it. Hold Command to push things along instead. A drag is never refused for lack of room.
pros: Works the way Premiere and Final Cut do
One rule to learn, and it is the one a dropped file already follows
cons: A careless drop can cover part of a clip you cut
options.mitigation: Undo brings it back in one press, and the bar over the tracks says Overwrite before you let go.

options.label: It goes up onto a new track, every way in
options.summary: Nothing is ever covered. Whatever way a clip arrives, if its spot is taken it lands on a new track over it. A dropped file stops covering what is there, and a dragged clip goes up a track instead of being refused.
pros: Nothing you cut is ever hidden or trimmed by a landing
cons: The timeline grows a track for every landing that overlaps
options.mitigation: An empty track can be removed from its right-click menu.

options.label: Keep the three rules as they are
options.summary: A dropped file covers, a paste or Option-drag copy goes up a track, and a dragged clip is refused with no room.
cons: The same spot does three different things depending on how you got there
